page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What ABA does
steps.margin_note: Name the hormone and the ion it moves. Three lines.
lines: ABA is abscisic acid, the stress hormone of
Under water stress, ABA drives K+ ions OUT of
steps.why: ABA acts on the same potassium pump that opens the pore in light, so a single hormone can override the light signal.
common_mistakes: Saying ABA closes the pore directly. It acts through the K+ ions.
Naming the wrong ion. It is POTASSIUM (K+) that leaves.
steps.memory_tip: ABA pulls the potassium out, and the pore follows.

steps.label: Why the pore closes
steps.margin_note: Four steps in order: ion, water potential, turgor, shape.

lines.text: Potassium out, water out, pore shut

lines: As K+ leaves, the water potential of the guard
Water moves out and the guard cells lose
The pair straightens and the stomata close, so
steps.why: The chain from ion to water to turgor to shape is the same one that opens the pore, run in reverse — which is why only the first step needed a hormone.
common_mistakes: Skipping straight from ABA to closure. The water potential and turgor steps are the mark.
Saying the guard cells become turgid. They LOSE turgor, which is why the pore shuts.
steps.memory_tip: Lose the water, lose the bend, lose the pore.
